Your HRV is at a solid 51 ms with no reported fatigue, indicating you are fully recovered and prime to absorb training stress, though your current fitness state is well below your target CTL of 60.

This represents an under-training phase. While recovery is optimal, the lack of acute stimulus means we need to aggressively rebuild volume and consistency without violating safe ramp rates (+1 to +2 CTL/week).

Peak cycling power and FTP are established, but long-term aerobic conditioning and running consistency require a strictly enforced pyramidal approach (70/30) to lock in gains across both cycling and your 5km running goals.
coach_verdict: Given your fresh recovery state and low acute fatigue, Priority 1 is the clear winner today: execute a structured Zone 2 aerobic base builder on the bike or run to increase volume safely while strictly adhering to the 70/30 pyramidal distribution rule.

priority_1.workout_details: 60 minutes continuous riding. Keep cadence high (90-95 rpm) with strict heart rate caps below Zone 3. Focus on smooth pedal strokes.
priority_1.reason: Highest priority because your 3-week volume is critically low and HRV/recovery status supports steady aerobic work to safely rebuild CTL.

priority_2.workout_details: 30-40 minutes easy jog. Include 4x 30-second strides at the end to maintain neuromuscular speed for your 5km goal without accumulating undue fatigue.
priority_2.reason: Directly targets your 5km running milestone while keeping intensity low to respect the pyramidal baseline requirements.

priority_3.workout_details: Squats (3x5 @ 70% 1RM), Romanian Deadlifts (3x8), Overhead Press (3x8), and Plank/Ab wheel supersets (3 sets to near failure).
priority_3.reason: Secondary option to build cycling torque and running power and support upper-body aesthetics, but secondary to the urgent need for aerobic volume.
